name: opendetex
desc: Tool to strip TeX or LaTeX commands from documents
why: A small, old tool that strips TeX commands from text, a neat transform of markup back into prose, though fairly modest.

brief.what_it_is: OpenDetex is a command-line filter that removes TeX and LaTeX markup from a text file and leaves the prose behind. It reads a TeX or LaTeX source file and writes plain text to output. It recognizes \input, \include and \includeonly, and it assumes LaTeX input when it sees the string \begin{document}. It ships two executables, detex and delatex, and delatex forces LaTeX mode.
brief.why_it_exists: The README describes it as a program to remove TeX constructs from a text file. It is a fork of Daniel Trinkle's detex 2.8, which OpenDetex's author, Piotr Kubowicz, maintains on GitHub.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the mechanism in detail. The ChangeLog says the scanner is written in Lex/Flex (detex.l), with a pre-generated detex.c distributed so the program can be built without Flex. Per the ChangeLog, control sequences are removed rather than replaced by spaces, and environments such as math, verbatim and figure can be ignored.

brief.install_notes: Build from source. You need make, a C compiler such as Clang or GCC, and a lex implementation such as flex. The INSTALL file says Debian/Ubuntu users can get these with sudo apt-get install make gcc flex, then run make and sudo make install. The distributed detex.c lets you build without Flex. No accounts, runtimes or first-run configuration are mentioned. detex.h holds global definitions that the README says should be edited to suit the local installation.
brief.standout: It is a small, old-school C tool that turns LaTeX back into readable prose, and its history runs from 1986 through the 2.8 series. The ChangeLog shows a practical touch: version 2.8.3 added a -r option that replaces math environments with nouns and verbs so sentences stay readable.
brief.status: maintained. The README header says version 2.8.13 UNRELEASED, and the ChangeLog lists releases through 2.8.12 with bug-fix entries in 2023 and later. I could not see commit dates or release tags. The 2.8.12 entry is dated 'October, 2026', which looks wrong, so the dates may be unreliable.
brief.caveats: The README and INSTALL mention only Unix-style build tooling. The ChangeLog records past Flex problems and a Cygwin fix, and removes OS/2 special files because their compilers no longer exist. The README mentions only \input, \include and \includeonly, so most of the TeX constructs it handles are not in the README. Licence is the NCSA/University of Illinois Open Source License. The homepage is the GitHub repo.
quotes: OpenDetex is a program to remove TeX constructs from a text file.
This program assumes it is dealing with LaTeX input if it sees the string "\begin{document}" in the text.
You can check for latest version, submit bug reports or patches, or ask for becoming team member there.
